text:
maria: Running a set of nsys traces after the runtime prefetch/batcher change (PR 0f3a9c). Seeing repeated prefetch kernel bursts right before KV lookup, looks like batching boundary shift. :mag:

sanjay: can you paste the timeline? perfetto or nsys flame?

maria: uploaded two traces: before (the baseline) and after (head). Links below. The after trace has a cluster of small memcpy + prefetch ops between token steps 120-180.

elaine: is this the change that adjusted micro-batch cut heuristic to favor packing?

maria: yes — the heuristic now biases toward filling the batch up to 80% rather than 60% to improve throughput. but latency tail is worse.

maria: nsys command I used:
```
nsys profile --trace=nvtx,cuda,osrt,cupti --sample=none -o after_trace qemu-runner --profile-runtime
```

perf-bot: upload complete: https://perf.redwood/perfetto/trace/after_2065012345
ci-bot: baseline trace (good): https://perf.redwood/perfetto/trace/before_2059991111

taylor: quick compare notes: after has multiple short prefetch kernels (~200-400us) interleaved, baseline had a single consolidated prefetch (~1.2ms).

sanjay: that suggests kernel selector started picking smaller kernels. maybe the batcher is splitting work across more dispatches.

maria: started a quick git-bisect between 205f2a1 (good) and 0f3a9c4 (bad). current suspect range narrows to a couple commits touching batcher.py and kv_cache evict logic.

elaine: remind me the logic — when batcher hits fill_threshold it flushes. Did we change threshold math or add prefetch for partial batches?

maria: changed threshold from `>= 0.6` to `>= 0.8` and we added a prefetch kickoff when estimated tokens_remaining < 16. That prefetch call executes outside the main kernel and may introduce extra small kernels.

taylor: timeline snippet (human summary):
- baseline: KV lookup -> single prefetch kernel (1.2ms) -> main attention kernel
- after: KV lookup -> prefetch A (300us) -> memcpy small (50us) -> prefetch B (250us) -> main attention kernel (shifted)

elaine: small memcpy + multiple prefetchs = more kernel launches, more scheduling overhead on GPU. Could be causing the tail.

sanjay: does nsys show significant cudaLaunch overhead?

maria: yes, launch latency spikes appear correlated. Looking at the launch queue there are more entries with <1ms runtime each.

maria: I collected a perf counter summary:
```
Before: kernel_launches=142, avg_kernel_ms=2.1
After: kernel_launches=214, avg_kernel_ms=1.1
```

taylor: that matches. More kernels, lower avg time, but worse total due to overhead.

elaine: proposed quick fix: collapse prefetches for partial batches into a single aggregated prefetch when tokens_remaining < N, or move prefetch into main work kernel (if safe). Could also revert threshold change.

sanjay: for triage we should bisect to the smallest commit that introduced the extra launch. do we have nvprof or nvtx annotated builds to inspect which function call maps to which kernel?

maria: nvtx ranges are present. I mapped two kernel names: `kv_prefetch_small` and `kv_prefetch_frag` — both originate from new prefetching path in kv_cache.cpp introduced in commit 0f3a9c4.

maria: running `git bisect run` with a lightweight smoke test to collect kernel counts per run. script returns PASS/FAIL based on launch count delta.

maria: bisect result points to commit 0f3a9c4 as first bad — that commit added fragmented prefetch and the new threshold.

taylor: okay, plan: revert fragmented prefetch, keep threshold tweak behind a feature flag, run nsys compare again.

elaine: can we add a microbench that asserts number_of_prefetch_kernels <= 2 for typical batches? then guard CI to catch regressions.

maria: added a microbench ticket and a follow-up PR to aggregate prefetched ranges. will test tomorrow and re-run full perfetto trace.

maria: quick note: example command I used for comparing kernel timelines: `nsys stats --report=timeline after.qdrep | grep Launch` — helps count launches per iteration.

perf-bot: note: traced run with aggregated prefetch branch shows kernel_launches=148, avg_kernel_ms=2.0 — close to baseline.

maria: thanks all. filing a short postmortem in eng-runtime with links to traces and the bisect log. :thumbsup:
